summary: Re-tested /browse Extra Filters language-pill badge fix only. The unified isActive helper now correctly registers a single language (TEST 1 passes — French alone shows badge '1', a regression from iteration_1). However, the fix is incomplete: when MULTIPLE languages are selected the badge does not increment because Array.isArray branch returns a single boolean, contributing only +1 regardless of array length. TEST 2 (French+German) shows '1' (expected 2) and TEST 3 (FR+DE+Brunette) shows '2' (expected 3). TEST 4 (Clear all filters) passes — badge clears and gender pill remains active. Backend skipped per request.

issues: React hydration warnings persist: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' and '<span> cannot be a child of <select>'. Source is a `<span data-ve-dynamic="true" style={{display:'contents'}}>` wrapper injected around <option> children inside ExtraFilters.jsx Select component. Cosmetic but pollutes console; consider unwrapping or rendering options without the visual-edit tracking span.

action_items: Fix activeExtraCount in /app/frontend/src/pages/Browse.js to add filters.languages.length (not just +1 if non-empty). Concretely: const activeExtraCount = EXTRA_FILTER_KEYS.filter(isActive).length + (filters.languages?.length || 0); — then drop ALL_EXTRA_KEYS / drop the Array.isArray branch from isActive.
Optional: silence the <span>-in-<option>/<select> hydration warnings inside ExtraFilters.jsx Select component.
critical_code_review_comments: The current `Array.isArray(v) ? v.length > 0 : ...` collapses an array of N selections into a single contributory unit. The naming ALL_EXTRA_KEYS suggests one badge unit per key, but the spec treats each language pill as its own unit — those two intents conflict. Either keep one-unit-per-key semantics (then update spec) or change to a sum-based count. The user's explicit spec mandates the latter.

filters state shape couples scalar fields (string) and array fields (languages) but the count derivation treats them uniformly via filter().length — guaranteed to under-count multi-select arrays. Future filters that become multi-select (e.g. services[]) will reproduce the same bug.

EXTRA_FILTER_KEYS is now duplicated by ALL_EXTRA_KEYS = [...EXTRA_FILTER_KEYS, 'languages']; merging them is fine but no longer needed once the formula is split. Remove ALL_EXTRA_KEYS to avoid dead code.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After the formula is changed to sum array length, re-run the same 4 cases against /browse?v=6 (bump SW cache). Use data-testid selectors: extra-filters-toggle, extra-lang-french, extra-lang-german, extra-hair_color (HTML <select>, use select_option(value='Brunette')), clear-extra-filters, extra-filters-count. The hair_color in this build is a <select>, not pills, so query [data-testid='extra-hair_color'] then select_option(value='Brunette'). Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_browse_filters.py (31/31) untouched and still valid.
rca of the issue: Iteration_1 reported the languages contribution was missing entirely. The dev unified the formula via Array.isArray detection in isActive. That correctly resurrects the +1 contribution for the WHOLE array, fixing the 'French alone shows no badge' symptom. But the spec requires per-pill counting, which Array.isArray-as-boolean cannot express. Reproduction (verified live): /browse → Extra Filters → click French (badge=1 OK) → click German (badge stays 1, expected 2). Mitigation: replace `const activeExtraCount = ALL_EXTRA_KEYS.filter(isActive).length;` with `const activeExtraCount = EXTRA_FILTER_KEYS.filter(isActive).length + (filters.languages?.length || 0);` and drop ALL_EXTRA_KEYS plus the Array.isArray branch in isActive.
